title: Learning Where and What to Lift for Bi-planar X-ray-to-CT Reconstruction
abstract: arXiv:2608.17255v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: X-ray imaging can be approximately modeled as the projection of an underlying volumetric attenuation field, with each measurement recording the accumulated attenuation along a corresponding ray path. Reconstructing a CT volume from only a few X-ray views is therefore severely ill-posed, as the projections collapse depth information and leave 3D locations of anatomical regions and their corresponding intensity distributions highly entangled and ambiguous. We observe that once the spatial organization of anatomical regions is established, estimating their CT intensities becomes substantially more tractable. Motivated by this, we propose LiftXR, an interleaved, geometry-guided framework that explicitly incorporates spatial layout recovery into CT reconstruction. translated_title: 学习在双平面X光到CT重建中何处及如何提升
translated_abstract: X射线成像可以近似建模为底层体积衰减场的投影，每次测量记录沿相应射线路径的累积衰减。因此，仅从少数X射线视图重建CT体积是严重不适定的，因为投影压缩了深度信息，使得解剖区域的3D位置及其对应的强度分布高度纠缠和模糊。我们观察到，一旦建立了解剖区域的空间组织，估计其CT强度就变得明显更容易处理。受此启发，我们提出了LiftXR，一个交错式、几何引导的框架，明确将空间布局恢复纳入CT重建。具体来说，一个布局提升器首先从双平面X射线生成3D解剖布局，为强度渲染器提供空间指导，以重建CT体积。
tldr: 本文提出LiftXR框架，通过交错式几何引导，先恢复3D解剖布局再估计强度，从而有效解决双平面X光到CT重建中的不适定问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes LiftXR, an interleaved geometry-guided framework that first recovers 3D anatomical layout and then estimates intensities, effectively addressing the ill-posed problem in bi-planar X-ray-to-CT reconstruction.
